pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
cons: Stock signal history lacks any independent review.
Ownership and regulatory oversight are not disclosed.
A broker markup is baked into each completed trade.
Several asset classes make the layout feel cluttered.

faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$200 minimum.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

bottomLine: What we found is a real service wrapped in marketing that outruns its own fine print. Trade the service, not the marketing.
The scorecard settles at 4.6. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.

granite-equitorage.seoDescription: We reviewed Granite Equitorage for 2026: minimum deposit, claims, red flags and the scorecard. Read before you register.
granite-equitorage.deck: One platform, one US$300 entry, several claims that do not survive contact with its own fine print.
granite-equitorage.depositMethods: Debit/credit cards, PayPal, Skrill, bank transfer
intro: Granite Equitorage publishes a strong pitch and, a few clicks later, a set of qualifications that quietly change it. This review reads both in full.
Under the marketing is a working template: signup, US$300 funding, configuration, then automatic or manual trading across 10 assets with the demo running beside the live account.
We reviewed the public record: pricing, restrictions, support hours, payout wording and every claim in between. Where the record contradicts itself, the scorecard marks it down.
whatItClaims: Futures contracts as the home market, with signals tuned to contract rhythms.
Alerts include a recommended position size plus a clear point to exit.
Adjustable risk settings built directly into the signal workflow.
Free demo mirrors the live futures contract feed and risk settings.
Entry from $250, free registration, no platform fee and 24-hour withdrawals.
whatWeChecked: The futures focus: contracts positioned as the primary market, not an add-on.
The risk workflow: position size and abandonment point attached to each alert.
The leverage warning: small price moves can produce large losses.
The record question: contract signals unaudited and history still short.
The fee line: no platform charge, but a spread on every contract.
The operator gap: no regulator, licence or broker partner disclosed.

cons: Futures leverage can amplify losses quickly.

redFlags: Unnamed operator, regulator and broker partner.
Unaudited futures performance record.
Leveraged contracts carry outsized loss risk.
Which contracts are chosen, and why, is never explained.

faqs.q: Is Granite Equitorage safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
US$300, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

bottomLine: Granite Equitorage is a standard-issue AI trading desk with the usual strengths and the usual omissions. None of the omissions are dealbreakers - they are conditions.
The scorecard settles at 4.6. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.
